AUTHOR: Siddiqui
TITLE: Automatic fish species classification in underwater videos: Exploiting pre-trained deep neural network models to compensate for limited labelled data
REGION: Western Australia (Cape Naturaliste to Houtman Abrolhos), 2011-2013
SPECIES: 16 focal species (e.g. Pentapodus porosus, P. emeryii, Choerodon rubescens, Plectropomus leopardus, Lethrinus nebulosus, Coris auricularis, Pagrus auratus, Scombridae spp.) plus an 'other species' class
DATA: Own stereo-BRUV footage (WA sampling programs); additional experiment on LifeCLEF 2015 Fish (Fish4Knowledge)
V_EV: Study area: 'Videos were collected from kelp, seagrass, sand and coral reef habitats between 5 and 50 m of water depth.'
D2: 1309/237/663 images (train/val/test, Table 1); allocation method not stated. LifeCLEF15 experiment: random 5% train / 5% val / 90% test per class
D_EV: no statement found on how images (extracted from 10-s clips) were allocated to training/validation/test sets; Table 1 gives counts only
R_EV: Discussion: 'we only trained the SVM (for classification) on features extracted by the same pre-trained ResNet-152b with cross-layer pooling on the images of LifeClef'15 images.'
C_EV: Classification of pre-cropped stills only: 'A one-vs.-all linear SVM was trained on the cross-pooled features for classification of the fish species.'
E_EV: Results: 'A classification accuracy of 94.3% was achieved when classifying only the 16 fish species which we focussed on for this trial.'
ARCH: ImageNet-pretrained CNN features (AlexNet, VGGNet, ResNet-152) with cross-layer pooling + one-vs-all linear SVM
NOTE: Main-dataset train/val/test allocation is never described (images extracted from 50-120 ten-second clips per species), so D1=NR; frames from the same clip may span splits (not discussed). LifeCLEF15 experiment retrains the SVM on LifeCLEF images (random 5% per class), so it is a second in-domain benchmark, not external testing (R1=N). The 'other species' class is a trained catch-all class, not a reject/unsure mechanism; treated as no score threshold so C_ALL=NA (verifier may consider). Depth 5-50 m and daylight deployments reported; murkiness described only qualitatively. Better LifeCLEF15 accuracy attributed qualitatively to 'relatively clear images' (cross-dataset, not stratified), V6=N. Clip counts given only as a range per species, NVID=NR.
